hits.title: Raytheon Technologies unveils RAIVEN - Intelligence Community News
hits.snippet: On April 24, Raytheon Technologies of Arlington, VA announced the launch of RAIVEN, a revolutionary electro-optical intelligent-sensing capability, which will enable pilots to have faster and more precise threat identification. Products & Services · Raytheon Technologies unveils RAIVEN · Company News · August 14, 2026 · Biz Opps · August 14, 2026 · Intel Agencies · August 14, 2026 · By Loren Blinde April 25, 2023 · 0 Comments · RAIVEN’s ‘intelligent-sensing’ capability uses artificial intelligence, hyperspectral imaging, and light detection and ranging, or LiDAR, to enable operators to see up to five times farther and clearer than traditional optical imaging. RAIVEN can identify objects optically and spectrally simultaneously in real-time — a single electro-optical/infrared, or EO/IR, system has never been able to do this before. Paired with AI, RAIVEN synthesizes reams of data into a detailed picture of the battlespace and the threats within it.

hits.snippet: The RAIVEN EO/IR product family is configurable and can support up to a spherical 360-degree field of view, which significantly improves the speed and accuracy of object detection, recognition and identification. The RAIVEN product family of next-generation electro-optical and infrared solutions are platform agnostic, scalable and customizable for missions across air, ground and sea. Caption ... ARLINGTON, Va., April 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has successfully completed the first flight test of its RAIVEN® Staring system, an air-cooled sensor suite that delivers greater situational awareness and operator survivability, on a UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter. The RAIVEN EO/IR product family is configurable and can support up to a spherical 360-degree field of view, which significantly improves the speed and accuracy of object detection, recognition and identification. This provides operators with increased visibility in a variety of degraded visual environments, terrains and battle scenarios. The sensors are produced in McKinney, Texas.
